text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"A subjective request for a recommendation and rationale about which player to build a team around, not a request for new data.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"scalar","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"That's a judgment call rather than something the data alone can answer, but based on the 2017 per-game numbers we pulled: James Harden led in scoring (30.08 ppg) while also contributing strong assists (9.79 apg), showing he can both score and create for teammates. Russell Westbrook posted a near triple-double average (29.03 ppg, 10.14 rpg, 10.02 apg), the most well-rounded statistical profile of the three, making him a strong build-around pick if you value versatility across scoring, rebounding, and playmaking. LeBron James, while slightly behind in scoring (28.20 ppg), still rebounded well (8.76 rpg) and distributed (8.70 apg) at a high level with great consistency (100 games played, the most of the group). If the priority is a single dominant scorer, Harden is the pick; if you want the most balanced two-way, do-everything player, Westbrook's stat line stands out. I'd lean toward Westbrook for building a team around, given his balance across all three major categories, but this is ultimately a basketball philosophy decision the numbers can inform, not settle outright."}
